Rioel Aotearoa

Nationwide NZ short-term rental intelligence, built on 51,096 real listings across all 67 territorial authorities.

About us

Rioel Aotearoa is a decision-support platform built on a nationwide data warehouse of 51,096 New Zealand short-term rental listings. It brings pricing, supply, availability and data-quality evidence together in one governed view, so that hosts, property managers and tourism boards can benchmark performance by ward, assess market opportunity and base pricing and investment decisions on transparent, traceable figures. It is an analytical tool, not a booking service, and it does not represent live Airbnb pricing.

What format? A plain CSV file (the format every spreadsheet app, including Excel, Google Sheets and Numbers, saves to via "Save As / Export → CSV"). Method and governance

How the warehouse was built and kept honest

The pipeline, the storage decision, the risks and the limits, as set out in the project report.

ETL pipeline 4 SCRIPTS, 4 GATES

Four commented Python scripts carry the Inside Airbnb files into a SQLite star schema. Every stage ends in a control that logs the error and stops the run, so nothing is quietly patched.

Sources
Listings51,096 rows × 18 columns
Reviews3,472,029 review events
Calendar18,733,644 listing-days
Ward reference239 rows × 2 columns
I01_extract_sources.py

Reads Listings and wards; chunk-reads Reviews and Calendar; profiles every file.

GateMissing-file check; duplicate-ID and missing-price checks; manifest and log.
II02_transform_listings.py

Builds the dimensions and fact_listings; derives price bands and the imputation flag.

GateType and geography checks; 51,096-row assertion.
III03_transform_temporal.py

Aggregates review events and calendar days to listing-month; extends date keys.

GateListing-universe restriction; complete-key check; duplicate-key control.
IV04_load_warehouse.py

Rebuilds SQLite from the DDL; loads the dimensions first, then the facts.

GateRow counts; orphan checks; SQLite integrity check.
Warehouse

Three facts, four dimensions. fact_listings holds one row per listing. The two monthly facts hold one row per listing per month, keyed on listing_id and date_id, so a duplicate month cannot be stored.

Calendar reduced about 29-fold. 18.7 million listing-days become 649,337 listing-months before they meet the listings, which stops silent row multiplication.

Post-load results. Zero duplicate keys, zero orphans, SQLite integrity check passed.

Storage and management evaluation 3 METHODS COMPARED

A repeated-aggregation workload over a 51,096-row fact table and about 1.7 million monthly rows, tested against three ways of storing it.

Not for core store

Why relational for now

Scalability is sufficient. The largest table has no more than 1.1 million rows after aggregation.
Access is easy. Analysts query it with standard SQL and Power BI.
It meets the business need. The questions are about stable, comparable aggregates, not real-time transactions.

The same logical schema moves to a managed cloud warehouse when users, refresh frequency or retained snapshots grow. Assessment synthesised from vendor documentation and Cattell (2011).

Risk identification and management 6 RISKS

Risks were identified against the DAMA-DMBOK framework and the ISO 8000-61 process model. The main integration risk is silent row multiplication when daily data is joined to listings. The control is to aggregate before joining and to test composite keys.

Integrity controls are good and security controls are moderate. Every integrity check passed in the prototype. A production deployment of automated pricing actions would also need role-based access, audit trails, encryption, retention policies, human approval and fairness testing.

Limitations to read before quoting a figure

One snapshot. Trends cannot be shown, and findings are descriptive.
Advertised prices. Prices are not transacted prices.
Proxies. Calendar unavailability can mean owner blocking, maintenance or a booking, so availability, occupancy and modelled revenue are indicators only.
Thin detail. Only 3,428 listings (6.7%) have detailed attributes.
Imputation. The 10.7% of prices filled with the ward median understate dispersion.
Design-level security. Controls are untested in production, and SQLite does not support concurrency.
Sources: listings_3.csv (n=51,096, nationwide, primary) integrated with the Inside Airbnb reviews and calendar exports and a detailed-attributes extract (3,428 listings matched by listing ID) and neighbourhoods_1.csv (239 NZ wards, reference) via ETL star schema.
